case_name: Hindustan Paper Corporation v Purnendu Chakrobarty and Others
facts: The appellant-Corporation on January 5, 1989 passed an order invoking Rule 23(vi) E of the Hindustan Paper Corporation Conduct Discipline and Appeal Rules.
The first respondent entered the services of the appellant as a Fire Fighting Officer and was eventually promoted on 28.8.1985 as Assistant Manager (Security & Fire- fighting).
On may 26, 1988 the body of one shanti Rani Chakrabarty, sister-in-law of the first respondent, was found in the house of the first respondent.
The first respondent applied casual leave on 27.5.1988 and an FIR was lodged against him and others under Section 302/201 read with Section 34 IPC by Karim Ganj Police.

On 3.6.1988 the first respondent after the expiry of casual leave sent an application for Earned Leave for 11 days giving the reason 'personal affair' and mentioning his leave address as U/S PWD Dispur, Gauhati.
The appellant-Corporation informed the police that the whereabouts of the first respondent were not known.
The permanent address of the first respondent as available in the official record was supplied to the police.

The appellant-Corporation sent series of leave applications dated 21.6.88, 14.7.88, 13.9.88, 28.8.88, 13.9.88, 29.9.88, 16.10.88 and 5.11.88 without minding to find out whether previous applications for leave have been sanctioned or not.

The first respondent submitted his reply baldly stating that he was suffering from chest pain for quite some time and that he had consulted specialist outside HPC for personal reasons and due medical certificate will be produced at the time of joining.
issues: What is the validity of Rule 23(vi) E of the Hindustan Paper Corporation Conduct Discipline and Appeal Rules?
Can an employee's leave applications be deemed unauthorized if they are not supported by medical certificates?
petitioner_arguments: The first respondent was suffering from chest pain for quite some time and had consulted specialist outside HPC for personal reasons.
He would produce medical certificates at the time of joining.
He knew that he was required to appear before the Police and would report to the police as per rules.
respondent_arguments: The Rule 23(vi) E has to be construed by reading into it the Principles of natural justice.
The first respondent's leave applications were not in proper form and were not supported by any medical certificates to justify his claim.
He did not reply properly by enclosing the medical certificates or come forward with a true case.
court_reasoning: The Rule 23(vi) E has to be construed by reading into it the Principles of natural justice.
The first respondent's attitude was expected to take the leave ordinarily with prior sanction and extend the same after the earlier one was sanctioned by the appropriate authority.
He did not reply properly by enclosing the medical certificates or come forward with a true case.
holding: The order passed by the appellant-Corporation invoking Rule 23(vi) E is set aside and the first respondent is reinstated with 50% back wages.
